title: Preventing SQL Injection in Java JDBC and JPA/Hibernate
content: In Java JDBC, building SQL strings with string concatenation (+ operators or StringBuilder) exposes applications to SQL injection. Using java.sql.PreparedStatement ensures SQL syntax and user data are separated at the database engine level.
remediation_guidelines: Always use java.sql.PreparedStatement with parameter index placeholders (?).
In JPA/Hibernate, use named parameters (:param) instead of string concatenation in JPQL/HQL queries.

title: Preventing Path Traversal in Java File I/O
content: Accepting unvalidated filenames in Java File or java.nio.file.Path constructors allows directory traversal sequences (../ or ..\) to access files outside the intended root directory. Validating the canonical path or using Path.normalize() and startsWith() prevents path traversal.
vulnerable_example:
File file = new File("/var/uploads/" + request.getParameter("filename"));
FileInputStream fis = new FileInputStream(file);
remediation_guidelines: Normalize and resolve paths against a safe root directory using java.nio.file.Path.
Check that the resolved path startsWith() the normalized base directory.
Never trust raw filenames supplied by clients without sanitization.

title: Safe Deserialization in Java
content: Java standard serialization via java.io.ObjectInputStream allows arbitrary object graphs to be deserialized, triggering gadget chains (e.g. Apache Commons Collections) that lead to remote arbitrary code execution.
vulnerable_example:
ObjectInputStream ois = new ObjectInputStream(clientSocket.getInputStream());
Object obj = ois.readObject(); // Vulnerable to gadget chains
remediation_guidelines: Avoid ObjectInputStream whenever possible; use JSON, Protobuf, or XML with safe parsers.
If native Java serialization is required, implement an ObjectInputFilter allowlist.
